Readers stay readers

A woman downloads “Where to start”, feels seen, and then has two options: book a call about coaching, or do nothing. Most choose nothing, and earn you nothing.

No filter

Free calls with people who aren’t ready

With no application in front of the call, your calendar fills with women who are still in the thick of it, or can’t invest yet. Your best hours go to the wrong conversations.

Tied to your time

Every new client costs you hours

Today each client comes from you personally: a post, a workshop, a call. There’s no product doing the first step for you while you coach.

The women who aren’t ready for coaching today leave with a free guide, and nothing that moves them towards you.

Sound familiar?

Everyone says “move on”. Nobody says how.

  • The plan you had doesn’t fit anymore, and the new one isn’t clear yet.
  • Some days hold grief and a to-do list at the same time.
  • People mean well, but “at least” and “everything happens for a reason” don’t help.
  • You want to feel hopeful again without pretending nothing happened.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five short lessons, at your own pace

Name the change

Put words to what ended, what shifted and what you’re still carrying, so it stops running in the background.

Make room for grief

Why grief and goals can sit side by side, and simple ways to give the hard feelings space without letting them run the day.

Take stock of who you are now

Your values, strengths and non-negotiables after the change, not before it.

Design what’s next

Sketch a next chapter that feels true, in small steps instead of one giant leap.

Your first 30 days

Turn it into a 30-day plan you can keep, even on the hard days.

Questions

Before you start

Is it too soon for this?

The kit moves at your pace. Some women start the week things change, others months later. You can pause any time.

Is this therapy?

No. It’s coaching and education with practical tools. It isn’t therapy or medical advice and doesn’t replace working with a licensed professional.

How long does it take?

Each lesson is short. Most women go through the kit in a week or two, then use the 30-day planner.

Why is it only $27?

Because the first step should be easy to take. Start here, and decide later if you want more support.

Script 1 · “Grief and goals”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Can grief and goals live in the same week? I think they have to.”

Body

“When life changes in a way nobody chose, most advice asks women to pick one: heal first, plan later. But real life doesn’t wait. Some days hold both. The Next Chapter Kit is five short lessons that help with both at once, at whatever pace feels right.”

CTA

“It’s $27, and it’s the first thing I’d hand a friend in that season. Tap Learn more.”

Shot: Abbie talking to camera, warm light, soft pink on-screen text “grief + goals”.

Script 2 · “Just move on”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“‘Just move on.’ Three of the least helpful words after a big change.”

Body

“Because nobody ever says how. Moving forward after a chapter ends isn’t about forgetting it. It’s about naming what changed, making room for what it cost, and then designing what’s next in small, doable steps.”

CTA

“I put those steps into a kit: five lessons, a workbook and a 30-day plan, for $27. Tap Learn more.”

Shot: talking to camera, on-screen text crossing out “just move on”.

Script 3 · “Where to start”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“The question I hear most from women in the middle of a life change: where do I even start?”

Body

“Not with a five-year plan. Start by writing down what actually changed. Then what you still want. Then one small step for the next 30 days. That’s it. Most people skip the first step and wonder why nothing sticks.”

CTA

“The Next Chapter Kit walks through all three, gently. $27. Tap Learn more to start today.”

Shot: talking to camera, cut to a hand writing three lines in the workbook.
